title: India's security policy not shaped by social media pressure, says Nishikant Dubey amid Starlink row
key_facts: Nishikant Dubey, a Bharatiya Janata Party MP who chairs India's Parliamentary Standing Committee on Information Technology, said on Sunday (11 Oct 2026) that India does not frame its security policy under pressure from social media or external influences.
He was responding to Elon Musk's criticism of resistance to the entry of Musk's satellite internet service Starlink into the Indian market.

Dubey said his committee had examined the security concerns about Starlink and that the Ministries of Defence and Home Affairs and investigation agencies had raised concerns about what he called 'dangerous games'.
He claimed the Congress-led government had flagged similar concerns in 2013-14 but did not elaborate on the alleged threats.

He rejected suggestions that financial considerations influenced policy: 'If our policy were driven by money, we would have rolled out the red carpet for you despite opposition from the security agencies'.
He told Musk: 'First, provide connections to the poor in your own country, America, at affordable rates, and then level accusations'.
quote_evidence: India does not frame its security policy under pressure from social media or any external influences, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP Nishikant Dubey, who chairs the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Information Technology, said on Sunday, responding to billionaire businessman Elon Musk's criticism of resistance to his satellite internet service Starlink's entry into the Indian market.
"If our policy were driven by money, we would have rolled out the red carpet for you despite opposition from the security agencies," he said.
"First, provide connections to the poor in your own country, America, at affordable rates, and then level accusations."
why_it_matters_hint: An Indian parliamentary committee chair answers Musk and defends the security objections that are holding up Starlink in India, without detailing the threats.
